text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Tuesday.

LONDON - British stocks ended well below their early highs as early Wall Street losses coupled with a series of tax measures in Tuesday's British budget dragged the market below its early record levels. Hopes for a fiscally prudent budget pushed the FTSE 100 index of leading shares to an intraday record of 4,094.4 in early trading but closed just 13.8 points higher at 4,068.4 -- below its record close of 4,073.1 set Oct. 21.

FRANKFURT - The German DAX index of 30 leading shares ended market trade above the magic 2,800-point level for the first time ever, spurred on by another record on Wall Street overnight and a firmer dollar. The DAX index ended up 11.45 points at 2,810.64 points. In after-hours trade, the index rose 8.10 to 2,808.62.
PARIS - French shares ended with modest losses after a round of profit-taking, traders said. The market had been looking to consolidate after recent strong rises.

However, as Wall Street continues to climb, Paris is well supported and brokers are eyeing 2,300 on the CAC index in the coming weeks. A buy programme was lifting the Dow in the Paris late afternoon. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 2.06 points at 2,275.08.

ZURICH - Swiss shares closed lower on sagging UBS shares, which slid 3 percent following the bank's announcement that onetime extraordinary provisions of 3 billion Swiss francs would lead to a net loss of around 500 million francs in 1996.

Prices were also pressured by transactions linked to derivative trading, dealers said. Most traders voiced disappointment with the market's sluggish performance despite record levels on Wall Street. The all-share SPI fell 8.32 points to 2,477.08 points.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended higher, supported by a booming New York stock market and towed by blue-chip issues, brokers said. They said market participants were eager to see the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) "tankan" business sentiment survey, to be released Wednesday. At the end of the session, the Nikkei 225 was up 124.68 points at 21,418.25.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index charged to a record close, propelled amid heavy volume by a surge in banking shares and a continued bullish tone in the property sector. The index rose 245.94 points to close at 13,485.33 after hitting an intraday record high at 13,495.38.

SYDNEY - Australian shares closed weaker, a promising early rise eroded by lunch as sellers, worried about the effect of the stronger Australian dollar on the resource sector, took control of the market. The market barometer, the All Ordinaries index, ended 12.7 points weaker at 2,382, after touching a life high of 2408.9 in the morning session.
JOHANNESBURG - Investors bailed out of South African gold stocks as the bullion price continued weak, shaving nearly 3 percent off the index and taking it to its lowest closing level in 10 months.

But industrial shares were boosted by futures-related trade although dealers said were it not for this activity, the index would have ended flat on a lack of fresh factors. The stronger rand also helped gains in industrials, dealers said.
The gold index ended down 48.4 points at 1,572.9, its lowest since Jan. 19. The industrial index added 60.3 points to 8,015.4 points and the all-share index was up 30 points to 6,721.3 points.
